title: Absolute risk reduction: back-calculate group size (N = 1200)
vignette: A study compared drug A versus standard therapy in preventing recurrent pulmonary embolism (PE). The absolute risk reduction for drug A versus standard therapy was 4%. The incidence of recurrent PE in the standard therapy group was 6%. There were 24 patients who developed recurrent PE in the drug A group. How many total subjects were there in the drug A group?

clues.text: absolute risk reduction for drug A versus standard therapy was 4%
clues.note: ARR = event rate(control) - event rate(treatment). With ARR 4% and control 6%, the drug A (treatment) event rate = 6% - 4% = 2%.

clues.text: incidence of recurrent PE in the standard therapy group was 6%
clues.note: The control (standard therapy) event rate is 6%; subtracting the ARR gives the treatment event rate.

clues.text: 24 patients who developed recurrent PE in the drug A group
clues.note: With a 2% event rate in the drug A group, 24 events = 2% of the group -> total = 24 / 0.02 = 1200.

whatMatters: ARR = event rate(control) - event rate(treatment). So event rate in drug A = 6% - 4% = 2%. Since 24 recurrent PEs = 2% of the drug A group, total = 24 / 0.02 = 1200. Answer C.
strategy: Two steps: (1) ARR = control rate - treatment rate -> 4% = 6% - X -> treatment (drug A) rate = 2%. (2) Rate = events/total -> 0.02 = 24/N -> N = 24/0.02 = 1200. Reject 600 (using 4%), 900, 1500, etc. - which come from using the wrong event rate.

eliminations.label: 600 - uses 4% instead of 2% (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: 24 / 0.04 = 600, using the ARR (4%) as the event rate. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the ARR is not the treatment event rate; the drug A event rate is 6% - 4% = 2%. ✅ Correct if: the drug A event rate were 4%.

eliminations.label: 900 - not a consistent rate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: doesn't correspond to 24 events at the correct rate. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: 24/900 = 2.67%, not the derived 2% drug A rate. ✅ Correct if: never with these numbers.

eliminations.label: 1500 - wrong rate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: 24/1500 = 1.6%. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: doesn't match the 2% drug A event rate. ✅ Correct if: never with these numbers.

eliminations.label: 1800 - wrong rate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: 24/1800 = 1.33%. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: inconsistent with a 2% event rate. ✅ Correct if: never with these numbers.

eliminations.label: 2100 - wrong rate
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: 24/2100 = ~1.14%. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: inconsistent with 2%. ✅ Correct if: never with these numbers.

reasoning: 4% = 6% - event rate(drug A) -> event rate(drug A) = 2%
mechanism: ABSOLUTE RISK REDUCTION (ARR) is the difference in event (bad-outcome) rates between the control and treatment groups: ARR = event rate(control) - event rate(treatment). Here the control (standard therapy) recurrent-PE rate is 6% and the ARR is 4%, so the drug A (treatment) event rate = 6% - 4% = 2% (0.02). An event rate equals the number of events divided by the number of subjects in that arm: rate = events/N. Rearranged, N = events/rate = 24 / 0.02 = 1200. Thus the drug A group had 1200 subjects. (Related measures: relative risk reduction = ARR/control rate = 4%/6% = 67%; number needed to treat = 1/ARR = 1/0.04 = 25.) The common error is dividing 24 by the ARR (0.04) to get 600 - but the ARR is not the drug A event rate; you must first derive the 2% treatment event rate.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Biostat > ARR = event rate(control) - event rate(treatment); event rate = events/N; NNT = 1/ARR; relative risk reduction = ARR/control rate.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Derive drug A event rate (6%-4%=2%), then N = 24/0.02 = 1200.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on absolute risk reduction, event rate, NNT, or relative risk reduction? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: 600 uses the ARR (4%) as the event rate; the drug A rate is 2% (6%-4%).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: ARR = control rate - treatment rate; N = events/rate; NNT = 1/ARR.

keywords.front: Derive drug A event rate here

keywords.back: Dividing events by ARR (0.04) instead of the true event rate (0.02)

firstAid.detail: Biostat: ARR = control-treatment rate; N = events/rate = 1200.
Biostat > ARR, NNT (1/ARR), relative risk reduction.
Biostat > rate = events/subjects in that arm.

memoryHook: ARR is the gap between the two event rates: 6% minus 4% leaves drug A at 2% - and 24 events at 2% means 1200 people (not 600).
